cells.text: 1 · Which cells and genes. Keep every cell whose guide targets one of the 2,317 genes all six lines share, plus every non-targeting control; keep protein-coding genes only (HGNC, Ensembl IDs); refuse non-integer counts. X-Atlas's parquet batches go through extract_xatlas in the same file under the same rules.

cells.code:
def extract_h5ad(line, path, anchor, pcg):
    a = ad.read_h5ad(path, backed="r")
    obs = a.obs.copy(); var_ens = np.array([strip(e) for e in a.var_names]); a.file.close()
    cols = np.array([j for j, e in enumerate(var_ens) if e in pcg])
    var = pd.DataFrame({"ensembl_id": var_ens[cols], "symbol": [pcg[e] for e in var_ens[cols]]})
    gid, gene = obs["gene_id"].astype(str).map(strip), obs["gene"].astype(str)
    is_ctrl = (gene == "non-targeting").to_numpy()
    rows = np.flatnonzero(gid.isin(anchor).to_numpy() | is_ctrl)
    log(f"{line}: {len(rows):,} of {len(obs):,} cells; {len(cols):,} of {len(var_ens):,} genes protein-coding")
    chunks, obs_parts = [], []
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as h:
        X = h["X"]
        for start in range(0, X.shape[0], BLOCK):
            stop = min(start + BLOCK, X.shape[0])
            sel = rows[(rows >= start) & (rows < stop)]
            if len(sel) == 0:
                continue
            sub = X[start:stop][sel - start][:, cols]
            if not np.all(sub == np.round(sub)):
                raise ValueError(f"{line}: non-integral counts in rows {start}-{stop}")
            chunks.append(sp.csr_matrix(sub.astype(np.int32)))
            obs_parts.append(pd.DataFrame({
                "target_ens": np.where(is_ctrl[sel], "CONTROL", gid.to_numpy()[sel]),
                "target_sym": gene.to_numpy()[sel], "is_control": is_ctrl[sel],
                "batch": obs["gem_group"].astype(str).to_numpy()[sel],
                "umi_total": obs["UMI_count"].astype(float).to_numpy()[sel],
                "pct_mito": obs["mitopercent"].astype(float).to_numpy()[sel] * 100,
                "guide": obs["sgID_AB"].astype(str).to_numpy()[sel],
                "cell": np.asarray(obs.index)[sel]}))
            if (start // BLOCK) % 10 == 0:
                log(f"  {line}: rows {stop:,}/{X.shape[0]:,}")
    return chunks, obs_parts, var

cells.text: 2 · Normalise each cell. Counts per 10,000, then log(1 + x).

cells.code:
def lognorm_chunk(C):
    lib = np.asarray(C.sum(1)).ravel().astype(np.float64)
    N = sp.diags((1e4 / lib).astype(np.float32)) @ sp.csr_matrix(C, dtype=np.float32)
    L = N.copy(); L.data = np.log1p(L.data)
    return N, L

cells.text: 3 · The control reference. In K562, HCT116 and HEK293T the paper draws exactly 10,000 controls, stratified over 30 k-means clusters of the controls (§A.1); the other lines keep every control.

cells.code:
def stratified_pool(Xc, n=POOL_N, seed=SEED):
    """COMPASS §A.1 control subsample: PCA(20) -> k-means(30) -> proportional draw -> exact n."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    Z = PCA(n_components=20, random_state=seed).fit_transform(Xc - Xc.mean(0))
    lab = KMeans(n_clusters=30, n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit_predict(Z)
    pick = []
    for k in range(30):
        m = np.flatnonzero(lab == k)
        take = int(round(len(m) * n / len(lab)))
        pick.extend(rng.choice(m, min(take, len(m)), replace=False))
    pick = np.array(sorted(set(pick)))
    if len(pick) > n:
        pick = np.sort(rng.choice(pick, n, replace=False))
    elif len(pick) < n:
        rest = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(lab)), pick)
        pick = np.sort(np.concatenate([pick, rng.choice(rest, n - len(pick), replace=False)]))
    return pick

cells.text: 4 · The gene panel. Seurat normalised dispersion, as scanpy's flavor='seurat', streamed so no line has to fit in memory; the file checks itself against scanpy on a subsample. The group panel is the 2,000 genes most often called variable across the study group's lines.

cells.code:
def seurat_dispersion(st, n_bins=20):
    """scanpy flavor='seurat' normalised dispersion from per-gene mean/var of CP10k."""
    mean = st["mean"].to_numpy().copy(); var = st["var"].to_numpy()
    mean[mean == 0] = 1e-12
    disp = var / mean
    disp[disp == 0] = np.nan
    disp = np.log(disp)
    lmean = np.log1p(mean)
    df = pd.DataFrame({"means": lmean, "dispersions": disp})
    df["mean_bin"] = pd.cut(df["means"], bins=n_bins)
    g = df.groupby("mean_bin", observed=False)["dispersions"]
    mb, sb = g.mean(), g.std(ddof=1)
    one = sb.isnull()                          # scanpy: single-gene bins get mean 0, std 1
    sb[one.to_numpy()] = mb[one.to_numpy()]; mb[one.to_numpy()] = 0
    df["dispersions_norm"] = ((df["dispersions"].to_numpy() - mb[df["mean_bin"]].to_numpy())
                              / sb[df["mean_bin"]].to_numpy())
    return df["dispersions_norm"].to_numpy(), lmean

cells.text: 6 · The effect vector. A knockdown's mean minus the control reference's mean, on the group panel. This matrix, 2,317 knockdowns by 2,000 genes per line, is what COMPASS decomposes.

decomp.title: The split itself: typical response, strength, own part

cells.text: The typical response u is the average effect vector, scaled to length 1. A knockdown's strength β is how far its effect runs along u (a dot product); its own part is what is left. Exact linear algebra: no fitting, no parameters.

cells.code:
def shared_axis(responses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The cell line's shared response axis `u_c`, a unit vector.

    Estimated as the normalised mean response over the perturbations you have measured.
    This is the only place the size of your measured panel enters COMPASS, and it
    converges quickly: a few tens of perturbations is usually enough.

    responses: (n_perturbations, n_genes), already expressed as differences from control.
    """
    if responses.ndim != 2 or responses.shape[0] < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 perturbations to estimate an axis, got {responses.shape}")
    return normalize(responses.mean(axis=0))


def normalize(v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """v / ||v||, guarded so an all-zero vector does not produce NaNs."""
    return v / max(float(np.linalg.norm(v)), 1e-12)


def decompose(responses: np.ndarray, axis: np.ndarray):
    """Split responses into their loading on `axis` and the remainder orthogonal to it.

    Returns (beta, residual) with shapes (n_perturbations,) and (n_perturbations, n_genes).
    By construction `residual @ axis == 0`, so the two parts carry no shared information.
    """
    beta = responses @ axis
    residual = responses - beta[:, None] * axis[None, :]
    return beta, residual

cells.code:
def plate1(S):
    D = dec("RPE1"); u = D["u"]; Z = D["Z"]; b = D["beta"]; R = D["r"]; names = list(D["names"])
    order = np.argsort(-u)
    nrm = np.linalg.norm(Z, axis=1); cos = b / nrm; sym = np.array([S.get(n, n) for n in names])
    ribo = np.flatnonzero([s.startswith(("RPL", "RPS")) for s in sym])
    hi = ribo[np.argmax(b[ribo])]                                          # a ribosomal knockdown riding the axis
    big = np.flatnonzero(nrm > np.percentile(nrm, 70))                    # large responses only
    mid = big[np.argmin(np.abs(cos[big] ** 2 - 0.5))]                     # the one closest to half shared
    lo = big[np.argmin(np.abs(cos[big]))]                                 # the large one least on the axis
    ex = []
    for i, why in ((hi, "a ribosomal-protein knockdown: most of its response lies on the shared axis"),
                   (mid, "a perturbation that is half shared, half its own"),
                   (lo, "a large response that is almost entirely its own")):
        ex.append({"target": names[i], "symbol": str(sym[i]), "why": why, "beta": round(float(b[i]), 3), "norm": round(float(nrm[i]), 3),
                   "cos": round(float(cos[i]), 3), "frac_shared": round(float(cos[i] ** 2), 3),
                   "z": r4(Z[i][order]), "shared": r4((b[i] * u)[order]), "residual": r4(R[i][order])})
    genes = [S.get(g, g) for g in np.array(D["panel"])[order]]
    return {"line": "RPE1", "n_genes": len(u), "genes_in_order": genes, "u": r4(u[order]), "exemplars": ex,
            "beta_all": r3(b), "cos_all": r3(cos)}

cells.text: The scatter uses a different statistic from the rest of the page, because the paper's §2.4 does: a signed Mann–Whitney z per gene, a knockdown's cells against the control reference, over each line's own 5,000 most variable genes. Steps 1–5 of the shared chain feed it; step 6 does not.

cells.code:
def mw_z(Xcsc, obs, targets, ctrl):
    """Tie-corrected Mann-Whitney z (perturbation vs control pool) for every target x gene."""
    tpos = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(targets)}
    tid = np.array([tpos.get(t, -1) for t in obs.target_ens])
    pr = np.flatnonzero(tid >= 0); g = tid[pr]
    n1 = np.bincount(g, minlength=len(targets)).astype(float)
    cr = np.flatnonzero(ctrl); n0 = len(cr)
    rowpos = np.full(Xcsc.shape[0], -1); rowpos[pr] = np.arange(len(pr))
    cpos = np.full(Xcsc.shape[0], -1); cpos[cr] = np.arange(n0)
    W = np.empty((len(targets), Xcsc.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32)
    N = n1 + n0
    for j in range(Xcsc.shape[1]):
        lo, hi = Xcsc.indptr[j], Xcsc.indptr[j + 1]
        r, v = Xcsc.indices[lo:hi], Xcsc.data[lo:hi]
        c = np.zeros(n0, np.float32); m = cpos[r] >= 0; c[cpos[r[m]]] = v[m]
        x = np.zeros(len(pr), np.float32); m2 = rowpos[r] >= 0; x[rowpos[r[m2]]] = v[m2]
        cs = np.sort(c)
        less = np.searchsorted(cs, x, "left"); eq = np.searchsorted(cs, x, "right") - less
        U = np.bincount(g, weights=less + 0.5 * eq, minlength=len(targets))
        z0c = (c == 0).sum(); z0p = np.bincount(g, weights=(x == 0), minlength=len(targets))
        t = z0c + z0p
        tie = (t ** 3 - t) / np.maximum(N * (N - 1), 1)
        sd = np.sqrt(n1 * n0 / 12.0 * ((N + 1) - tie))
        W[:, j] = (U - n1 * n0 / 2.0) / np.maximum(sd, 1e-12)
    return W, n1

cells.text: Size and likeness. m is the length of a knockdown's z-vector; a is its correlation with the line's average z-vector; s is a one-dimensional Isomap of the two, turned so it rises with m.

cells.code:
for size in (1000, 2000, 5000):
        w = W[:, :size]
        wbar = w.mean(0)
        m = np.linalg.norm(w, axis=1)
        a = np.array([np.corrcoef(wi, wbar)[0, 1] for wi in w])
        rows[f"m_{size}"], rows[f"a_{size}"], rows[f"s_{size}"] = m, a, isomap_coord(a, m)

def isomap_coord(a, m):
    Z = np.column_stack([(a - a.mean()) / a.std(), (m - m.mean()) / m.std()])
    s = Isomap(n_neighbors=30, n_components=1).fit_transform(Z)[:, 0]
    return s if np.corrcoef(s, m)[0, 1] >= 0 else -s

cells.text: Do the six lines rank knockdowns alike? Kendall's coefficient of concordance, with the standard tie correction, on the paper-matched gene-name anchor and on our Ensembl anchor.

cells.code:
def kendalls_w(M):
    """Kendall's coefficient of concordance for an (items x raters) matrix, rank-based,
    with the standard tie correction."""
    from scipy.stats import rankdata
    n, m = M.shape
    Rk = np.column_stack([rankdata(M[:, j]) for j in range(m)])
    S = ((Rk.sum(1) - m * (n + 1) / 2) ** 2).sum()
    T = sum(((np.unique(Rk[:, j], return_counts=True)[1] ** 3 - np.unique(Rk[:, j], return_counts=True)[1]).sum()) for j in range(m))
    return 12 * S / (m ** 2 * (n ** 3 - n) - m * T)

cells.text: CompassX (Table 3), the authors' predictor: the hidden line contributes only its typical response; β and the own part come from the other lines. Scored two ways: de-biased Pearson against measured effects built from the other half of the controls (accuracy), and whether a prediction is closer to its own knockdown than to the others (PDS gain).

cells.code:
class CompassX(_Base):
    """Both components taken from other cell lines. Nearly independent of panel size.

    The target cell contributes only its shared axis. Everything perturbation-specific is
    donor-averaged, so predictions for a perturbation you have never measured in this cell
    are as good as for one you have, provided it was measured somewhere else.

    donor_beta, donor_residual: the loading and off-axis part for each perturbation,
        averaged over the donor cell lines, as dicts keyed by perturbation name.
    """

    def __init__(self, donor_beta: dict, donor_residual: dict):
        super().__init__()
        self.donor_beta = donor_beta
        self.donor_residual = donor_residual

    def _fit(self, responses):
        pass                      # nothing to learn beyond the axis

    def predict(self, perturbations):
        self._check_fitted()
        missing = [p for p in perturbations if p not in self.donor_beta]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"no donor measurement for {len(missing)} perturbation(s), "
                           f"e.g. {missing[:3]}; CompassX cannot predict these")
        beta = np.array([self.donor_beta[p] for p in perturbations], dtype=float)
        residual = np.array([self.donor_residual[p] for p in perturbations], dtype=float)
        return assemble(beta, residual, self.axis_)

def benchmark(target, donors, eff, panel, train_sizes=None, n_splits=5, seeds=None, rng_seed=SEED):
    """Table 3 (train_sizes None: 80/20) or Fig. 4 budget sweep (train_sizes list)."""
    names, pm, Z, Xpool = eff[target]
    dbeta, dres = donor_components([eff[d][2] for d in donors], names)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(rng_seed)
    halves = []
    for _ in range(N_HALVINGS):
        perm = rng.permutation(Xpool.shape[0]); h = len(perm) // 2
        halves.append((Xpool[perm[:h]].mean(0), Xpool[perm[h:]].mean(0)))
    rows = []
    settings = [(None, s) for s in range(n_splits)] if train_sizes is None else [(n, s) for n in train_sizes for s in range(seeds)]
    for n_train, s in settings:
        r = np.random.default_rng(rng_seed + 1000 * (n_train or 0) + s)
        perm = r.permutation(len(names))
        ntr = int(round(0.8 * len(names))) if n_train is None else n_train
        tr, te = perm[:ntr], perm[ntr:]
        te_names = [names[i] for i in te]
        src_avg = np.array([np.mean([eff[d][2][i] for d in donors], 0) for i in te])
        acc = {"CompassX": [], "training mean": [], "source average": []}
        for c1, c2 in halves:
            z1 = pm - c1; z2 = pm - c2                       # truth side / model side
            model = CompassX(dbeta, dres).fit(z2[tr], [names[i] for i in tr])
            preds = {"CompassX": model.predict(te_names),
                     "training mean": np.repeat(z2[tr].mean(0, keepdims=True), len(te), 0),
                     "source average": src_avg}
            for k, P in preds.items():
                acc[k].append(np.nanmean(rowwise_pearson(P, z1[te])))
        model = CompassX(dbeta, dres).fit(Z[tr], [names[i] for i in tr])
        full = {"CompassX": model.predict(te_names), "training mean": np.repeat(Z[tr].mean(0, keepdims=True), len(te), 0),
                "source average": src_avg}
        for k in acc:
            rows.append({"target": target, "n_train": ntr, "split": s, "method": k,
                         "debiased_pearson": float(np.mean(acc[k])),
                         "pds_gain": float(pds_gain(full[k], Z[te], te_names, panel))})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def pds_gain(pred, meas, names, panel):
    """Cosine PDS gain: for each prediction, rank of its own measured effect among the test pool."""
    col = {g: j for j, g in enumerate(panel)}
    dots = pred @ meas.T
    pn2 = (pred ** 2).sum(1); mn2 = (meas ** 2).sum(1)
    P = len(names); scores = np.empty(P)
    for i, t in enumerate(names):
        d = dots[i].copy(); a2 = pn2[i]; b2 = mn2.copy()
        j = col.get(t)
        if j is not None:                                  # drop the perturbed gene
            d -= pred[i, j] * meas[:, j]; a2 -= pred[i, j] ** 2; b2 -= meas[:, j] ** 2
        cos = d / np.sqrt(np.maximum(a2, 1e-24) * np.maximum(b2, 1e-24))
        k = (cos > cos[i]).sum()
        scores[i] = 1 - k / P
    return scores.mean() - 0.5

def rank_enrichment(values, genes, sets, min_size=10):
    """AUC of members vs non-members (rank-based, equivalent to Mann-Whitney U / n1 n0)."""
    r = rankdata(values); n = len(values); pos = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genes)}
    out = []
    for term, members in sets.items():
        idx = [pos[g] for g in members if g in pos]
        n1 = len(idx)
        if n1 < min_size or n1 > n - min_size:
            continue
        U = r[idx].sum() - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2; n0 = n - n1
        auc = U / (n1 * n0)
        z = (U - n1 * n0 / 2) / np.sqrt(n1 * n0 * (n + 1) / 12)
        out.append((term, n1, auc, z))
    df = pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["term", "n", "auc", "z"])
    from scipy.stats import norm
    df["p"] = 2 * norm.sf(np.abs(df.z)); df["q"] = multipletests(df.p, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    return df

        Xd = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(S)), S.to_numpy()])
        beta_ols, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xd, zu.to_numpy(), rcond=None)
        r2 = 1 - ((zu.to_numpy() - Xd @ beta_ols) ** 2).sum() / ((zu.to_numpy() - zu.mean()) ** 2).sum()
        hm = libs["MSigDB_Hallmark_2020"]
        H = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(zu))] + [zu.index.isin(list(v)).astype(float) for v in hm.values()])
        bh, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(H, zu.to_numpy(), rcond=None)
        r2h = 1 - ((zu.to_numpy() - H @ bh) ** 2).sum() / ((zu.to_numpy() - zu.mean()) ** 2).sum()
        summary[l] = {"genes": len(u), "R2_u_on_curated_signatures": float(r2), "R2_u_on_49_hallmarks": float(r2h)}

def classes(inst, idx):
    """Pairwise class labels among instances idx (different plates only)."""
    pl, wl, dr = inst.plate.values[idx], inst.well.values[idx], inst.drug.values[idx]
    iu = np.triu_indices(len(idx), 1)
    a, b = iu
    xp = pl[a] != pl[b]
    known = ~np.isnan(wl[a]) & ~np.isnan(wl[b])
    sw = known & (wl[a] == wl[b])
    dw = known & (wl[a] != wl[b])
    p13 = ~known
    sd = dr[a] == dr[b]
    t614 = ((pl[a] == 6) & (pl[b] == 14)) | ((pl[a] == 14) & (pl[b] == 6))
    return iu, dict(
        same_drug_same_well=xp & sd & sw & ~t614, same_drug_6_14=xp & sd & t614,

def summarise(V, inst, idx, tag):
    """Mean cosine per class for row-vectors V[idx]."""
    N = un(V[idx])
    C = N @ N.T
    iu, cls = classes(inst, idx)
    v = C[iu]
    return {f"{tag}|{k}": (float(v[m].mean()) if m.any() else np.nan, int(m.sum())) for k, m in cls.items()}

Two wells that should be the same. The difference of two no-drug wells, against the difference sampling alone would give at those cell counts; the excess is the noise between wells (τ²).

cells.code:
def pair_test(S, n, a, b, c, u=None, beta_drug_med=None):
    if min(n[a, c].min(), n[b, c].min()) < MIN_HALF:
        return None
    na, nb = n[a, c].sum(), n[b, c].sum()
    d = S[a, c].sum(0) / na - S[b, c].sum(0) / nb
    s2 = np.nanmean([s2_well(S, n, a, c), s2_well(S, n, b, c)])
    exp = np.sqrt(s2 * (1 / na + 1 / nb))
    nd = float(np.linalg.norm(d))
    raw_split = float(np.linalg.norm(S[a, c, 0] / n[a, c, 0] - S[a, c, 1] / n[a, c, 1]))
    out = {"cells_a": int(na), "cells_b": int(nb), "norm_diff": nd, "expected_sampling": float(exp),
           "diff_over_sampling": nd / exp, "raw_split_half_one_well": raw_split,
           "tau2": float(max(0.0, nd ** 2 - exp ** 2) / 2), "d": d}
    if u is not None:
        out.update({"beta_well": float(d @ u), "cos_diff_u": float(d @ u / nd),
                    "abs_beta_well_over_median_drug_beta": abs(float(d @ u)) / beta_drug_med if beta_drug_med else np.nan})
    return out
